1.
The defects pointed out by the Registry are overruled.

The petitioner is apprehending from arrest in connection with FIR No.12/2024 of Cyber Police Thane, District Brihanmumbai City Maharashtra for the offence under Sections 34, 406, 471, 420 & 120B of the IPC and Section 66 D of the IT Act.
Indisputably, the petitioner is seeking a transit bail for a limited period so that he can be able to take necessary steps to exercise his legitimate rights.

2. Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned Public Prosecutor and perused the material available on record.
3.
Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner is a permanent resident of Mahamandir, District Jodhpur in the [2024:RJ-JD:22245] (2 of 4) [CRLMB-6012/2024] State of Rajasthan.
He is an E-mitra operator.
In this case, the aforementioned FIR got lodged against some persons while alleging that the bank has issued credit cards after the verification of the documents.

Total 34 credit cards were issued and those persons have not returned the amount used through credit cards.
The case is related to misuse of credit card, cheating and misappropriation of property as well as impersonation.
It is further submitted that the petitioner is not named in the FIR but the police authority issued notice wrongly to him.
The petitioner is not the beneficiary in the matter.
He is willing to join the investigation and seeks interim protection from arrest so as to make him able to approach the Court at Mumbai.

4. Learned counsel for the petitioner further submits that although in view of the provisions contained in Sec.41 CrPC and the guiding principles enunciated by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Arnesh Kumar Singh Vs State of Bihar: 2013 (8) SCC 273, the arrest was not imperative yet the petitioner apprehends that the Maharashtra Police, in connivance with the complainant, may arrest him.

entities.text: Arnesh Kumar Singh Vs State of Bihar: 2013 (8) SCC 273
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He is desirous to approach the concerned Sessions Court and High Court of Mumbai for protection under Sec.438 CrPC yet apprehends that in the event he moves to that area, he can be arrested and therefore, a transit bail for a limited period may be granted to him.

Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that there are judicial pronouncements, ruling the notion that the other High Court can also grant interim protection from arrest to an accused till he approaches the competent court having territorial jurisdiction.

Reliance is placed on Banwari Lal Kushwah Vs State of Rajasthan:2014 (2) RLW 1849 (Raj) [2024:RJ-JD:22245] (3 of 4) [CRLMB-6012/2024] and Mahesh Kumar Sharma Vs State ofRajasthan, reported in 2005 WLC (Raj) UC 690.
5.

sentences.text: Per contra, learned Public Prosecutor opposed the bail.
However, he too does not dispute that this Court has jurisdiction to grant protection from arrest to the accused-petitioner outside the State for a limited period.

6. Considering the over all submissions and looking to totality of the facts & circumstances of the case, I deem it appropriate to grant transit bail to the petitioner, for a limited period of 30 days from today.

7. Accordingly, the bail application is allowed and it is directed that in the event of arrest of the petitioner- Madhusudan Maheshwari S/o Sh Satyanrayan Maheshwari, in connection with the FIR No.12/2024 of Cyber Police Thane, District Brihanmumbai City Maharashtra for the offence under Sections 34, 406, 471, 420 & 120B of the IPC and Section 66 D of the IT Act., he shall be released on bail forthwith, provided he furnishes a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (rupees Fifty Thousand) with two sureties in the sum of Rs.25,000/- (rupees Twenty Five Thousand) each, to the satisfaction of concerned Investigating Officer/SHO, for a period of 30 days from today.

8. It is made clear that the effect of the interim bail from arrest shall be for a limited period of 30 days from today and this interim bail stand ceased automatically after expiry of 30 days.
9.
Further, during the period of bail, the petitioner will not hamper the course of investigation and shall cooperate with the agency.
